region: Industry City, Sunset Park · Brooklyn, New York
about: Fort Hamilton Distillery is the Brooklyn whiskey house of Alex Clark, a veteran New York bartender, and his wife, Amy Grindeland, who founded it in 2016 to revive the Northeast’s pre-Prohibition whiskey traditions. The name honors the old army fort at Brooklyn’s southern tip, where the Battle of Brooklyn began in 1776. The distillery’s bar and tasting room sit in Industry City in Sunset Park, where some of the barrels also age.

Released in spring 2024, the Single Barrel Bourbon completed Fort Hamilton’s core range and is its most corn-forward whiskey: 85% corn, 10% rye and 5% malted barley, all grown at Migliorelli Farm in Tivoli, in the Hudson Valley. It is distilled at Taconic Distillery in Stanfordville on a 12-foot Vendome column still and aged in 30-gallon, number 3 char barrels. Clark chooses each barrel by hand, and it is bottled at 95 proof with no chill filtration, color or flavoring.

Fort Hamilton’s own notes describe toasted pecan, sage and lemon peel, then brioche crust and brown sugar, with a savory finish of olive oil and salt. Wine Enthusiast’s Kara Newman gave it 95 points, noting vanilla bean and caramel and a substantial, warming palate that opens toward cocoa, hazelnut and pecan pie with a little water.
